properties.title: OphthaDT: Generative Digital Twins for Forecasting Visual Acuity Trajectories in Ophthalmology

membership.reason: OphthaDT fine-tunes MedGemma 4B on serialized longitudinal clinical-trial records to forecast 100-week visual acuity (BCVA) trajectories.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 predictive longitudinal EHR/trial trajectory world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Fine-tuned MedGemma 4B over visit-by-visit serialized multimodal clinical-trial narratives

properties.flow: Multimodal ophthalmology trial history -> structured text serialization -> MedGemma 4B -> multi-horizon BCVA trajectory (up to 100 weeks)

properties.purpose: Long-horizon BCVA trajectory forecasting in nAMD and DME.
properties.environment: Four retrospective Phase III clinical trials (3,220 patients)

assertions.rationale: Text serialization encodes irregular visit intervals ('4 weeks later') without imputation.
Patient-level 80/10/10 split stratified by trial and indication.
MedGemma 4B LLM tokenizer/transformer over serialized clinical narratives.
Autoregressive LLM context representation over patient visit history.
Conditioned on full visit-by-visit baseline and treatment history.
Multi-horizon BCVA trajectory forecasting up to 100 weeks.

Multi-horizon BCVA forecasting (weeks 8, 24, 52, 100) is evaluated on the held-out 10% patient-level test split (Table 1 p. 3, Sec. 4 p. 4): lowest MAE across all horizons in nAMD (6.0% mean MAE reduction), while trailing the linear baseline in DME.
Ophthalmology clinical-trial simulation and personalized visual acuity forecasting.
Multi-horizon BCVA MAE up to 100 weeks (6.0% reduction in nAMD; outperforms RF/XGBoost in DME).
Evaluated across four Phase III clinical trials spanning nAMD and DME.

evidence_fragments.content: We introduce OphthaDT, an LLM-based digital twin for ophthalmology that serializes longitudinal patient histories from 3,220 patients across four Phase III clinical trials into structured narratives to forecast best corrected visual acuity (BCVA). In benchmarks spanning up to 100 weeks, OphthaDT demonstrated the lowest prediction error in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), achieving an average mean absolute error (MAE) reduction of 6.0% compared to all baselines.

Figure 1. OphthaDT pipeline overview. (1) Patient history and baseline measurements are extracted from four Phase III clinical trials. (2) Longitudinal records are serialized into structured text prompts with forecasting instructions. (3) MedGemma 4B is fine-tuned on instruction–completion pairs. (4) The model predicts BCVA trajectories for unseen patients.
The aggregated cohort was split at the patient level into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% test sets, stratified by clinical trial and indication (nAMD/DME).

In the nAMD cohort, OphthaDT achieved the lowest MAE across all forecasted timepoints, outperforming every evaluated baseline. Across the full 100-week horizon, the model demonstrated a mean error reduction of 5.7% relative to Random Forest and 2.1% relative to the linear model, averaging 6.0% across all three baselines.

capability_assessments.rationale: Autoregressive LLM forecasting longitudinal BCVA trajectories up to 100 weeks from serialized multimodal patient histories without action-conditioned counterfactual rollouts (L1).

limitations: Observational forecasting on retrospective Phase III trials without prospective deployment or counterfactual treatment comparisons.
notes: All 8 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 2 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: OphthaDT: Generative Digital Twins for Forecasting Visual Acuity Trajectories in Ophthalmology
legacy_cells.C: Belligoli, Pietro, Makarov, Nikita, Boushehri, Sayedali Shetab, Schmich, Fabian, Rodriguez-Esteban, Raul, Menden, Michael
legacy_cells.O: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD); diabetic macular edema (DME)
legacy_cells.S: Forecast future BCVA values at specified study weeks from a patient's baseline and longitudinal clinical history.
legacy_cells.T: 3,220 patients with nAMD and DME across four Phase III clinical trials; other inclusion criteria not reported.
legacy_cells.BS: Generated BCVA values as a structured text trajectory, decoded by a parser.
legacy_cells.BV: Masked next-token cross-entropy on target completion tokens.
legacy_cells.CG: 10 independently sampled trajectories per patient; element-wise mean used for final forecast.
legacy_cells.DY: MAE and R² reported at weeks 8, 24, 52, and 100 for nAMD and DME; Table 1 reports nAMD MAE 6.13 at week 8 and 9.82 at week 100.
legacy_cells.EG: Training on two NVIDIA H100 (80GB) GPUs took approximately 5 hours.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with Linear, Random Forest, and XGBoost; nAMD OphthaDT had lowest MAE across timepoints, while DME results were competitive (Table 1).
legacy_cells.FL: Serialized static baseline characteristics and chronological clinical-event history (including treatment records) are prompted to fine-tuned MedGemma 4B, which generates future BCVA values; no planner is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors list a serialization method for multimodal ophthalmic events, BCVA forecasting across extended horizons, and application of LLM trajectory modeling beyond oncology.
legacy_cells.FN: nAMD: lowest MAE across forecast timepoints and 6.0% average MAE reduction versus baselines; DME: competitive, with average MAE reductions of 2.6% versus Random Forest and 6.9% versus XGBoost.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state the implementation is limited to a specific subset of clinical variables.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose expanding the cohort and integrating OCT scans into the serialization pipeline.
legacy_cells.FQ: Applicability of structured-text LLM trajectory forecasting to non-oncology areas with different disease dynamics was described as unclear; ophthalmology remained underexplored.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is retrospective internal BCVA forecasting from trial histories; the paper does not demonstrate identified treatment effects, alternative future-action rollouts, planning/decision quality, external or prospective validation, or clinical utility outcomes.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
